suggested_experiment_name: NuSTAR X-ray observations of Quintuplet and Westerlund 1 super star clusters
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper reports a new measured exclusion limit on the axion-photon coupling g_agamma from NuSTAR observations of the Quintuplet and Westerlund 1 super star clusters. The limit is g_agamma ≲ 3.6 × 10^-12 GeV^-1 for axion masses m_a ≲ 5 × 10^-11 eV at 95% confidence. This is a mass-independent (flat) bound valid over the low-mass range stated, encoded as a horizontal line from 1e-11 eV to 5e-11 eV. The analysis uses archival NuSTAR data (10-80 keV) to search for X-ray signatures from axion conversion in Galactic magnetic fields. No significant evidence for axions was found. The coupling type is AxionPhoton because the paper constrains g_agamma, the axion-photon coupling constant. This is a stellar/astrophysical bound, not a haloscope dark matter search, so no local DM density is assumed. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.65, 30)) | Vision: Figure 3 shows 95% upper limits on g_agamma vs axion mass m_a from NuSTAR observations of Quintuplet and Westerlund 1 super star clusters. The plot compares constraints with CAST experiment and SN1987a limits. The lower boundary of the exclusion region (black curve labeled 'Joint 95% limit') traces the constraint. At low masses (m_a < 5×10^-11 eV), the limit is approximately flat at ~3.6×10^-12 GeV^-1. The boundary shows a gentle slope increase toward higher masses. The plot also shows expected limits under null hypothesis (dotted line) and 1σ/2σ bands (yellow/green). Confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the exact boundary pixels are somewhat difficult to resolve at the plot resolution, (2) the paper's main text states the joint limit as g_agamma ≲ 3.6×10^-12 GeV^-1 for m_a ≲ 5×10^-11 eV, which anchors the low-mass plateau, but precise intermediate mass values require careful visual interpolation.
